newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was generally firm on moderate demand and mostly moderate offerings, USDA said.

Choice product firmed up this week after a free fall of $14.88 per cwt on the light Choice cutout the three previous trading periods. Light Choice and Select spread now stands at $9.51 compared to its week ending high of $21.40 on Nov 21.

Retail and HRI demand was rather light for immediate needs. Forward interest, on the other hand, was fairly good especially on the chuck and round cuts, which trended higher throughout the trading period.

Loin cuts traded somewhat higher, especially on the Select cuts, as tenderloins continue to trade at high levels. Rib cuts traded lower as seasonal demand comes to a close. Closely trimmed items traded higher with the vast majority of the gains on the chuck and round cuts.

Trade on beef trimmings was weak on light to moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were steady to firm on light to moderate demand and offerings, with most of the advances on the fed cattle grinds.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal 1.00 to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal 2.00 higher; Select and Choice round primal 2.00 to 3.00 higher; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 3.00 higher; Closely trimmed items 1.50 to 2.50 higher; Beef trimmings 1.50 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 2.50 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.07 at 105.37; 700/850 Up .63 at 104.13; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.45 at 95.86; 700/850 Up 2.39 at 95.12.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The lean boneless beef market traded sharply higher this week on reduced offerings as inclement winter weather curtailed the movement of slaughter cows to market.

Additionally, being in the middle of the holiday shopping season, the limited availability stimulated demand which became moderate, especially for immediate grinding needs. However, the cow cuts were unevenly steady in limited trading.

Utility and Cutter carcasses not established; Fresh 90% boneless beef 7.00 higher in the Midwest, Texas 4.00 higher; 85% 5.00-5.50 higher; 75% steady; 65% firm. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, December 19, 1996 was estimated at 66.70 per cwt., up 3.75 from last week.
